name: Dorado
introduction: is the Dolphinfish, or Swordfish, a constellation introduced by Dutch navigators in the 1590s. It is faint, but it contains one of the most spectacular sights of the southern sky: most of the Large Magellanic Cloud.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: The Large Magellanic Cloud is a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way, about 160,000 light-years away, visible to the naked eye as a detached piece of the Milky Way. Within it lies the Tarantula Nebula, the most active star-forming region known in our Local Group of galaxies. Its central cluster, R136, contains some of the most massive stars ever found, more than 150 times the mass of the Sun.

In 1987, a supernova exploded in the Large Magellanic Cloud, the nearest seen since 1604. Detectors on Earth caught a burst of neutrinos from the collapsing star, opening a new window on how massive stars die.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Alpha Doradus](hip:21281) is a blue-white star with a peculiar, silicon-rich surface. [Beta Doradus](hip:26069) is a Cepheid variable that brightens and fades every 9.8 days. [Gamma Doradus](hip:19893), 67 light-years away, gives its name to a class of stars that pulsate gently by shifting their surfaces.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The south pole of the ecliptic lies in Dorado. Besides the Large Magellanic Cloud, the constellation includes several galaxies, such as the Dorado Group, a loose gathering of spirals and ellipticals.
